{{Top|fga}}
{{Quote|No being should be judged on his or her&mdash;or frankly, its&mdash;species, or what world they were born on. It is who you are that matters.|[[Chevin/Legends|Chevin]] [[Journalist/Legends|journalist]] [[Perre Needmo]]|<ref name="Allies">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Allies]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Herglic_with_aliens.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A member of the [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] species stands alongside members of the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]], [[Herglic/Legends|Herglic]], and [[H'nemthe (species)/Legends|H'nemthe]] species.]]
'''Species''' were unique groups of life forms, sharing a set of observable characteristics. Life forms varied in size from microscopic [[Bacteria/Legends|bacteria]], to enormous [[Exogorth/Legends|Exogorths]] of deep space and [[Hemes Arbora|living planets]]. Of only sentient species there were over 20 million known kinds.<ref name="TBH">''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]'', p301.</ref><ref name="LOS">{{StoryCite|story=The Last One Standing|book=Legacy of the Jedi/Secrets of the Jedi omnibus|text=''Legacy of the Jedi/Secrets of the Jedi'' omnibus}}</ref> [[Sentience/Legends|Sentient]] species were sometimes erroneously referred to as ''races'', which more accurately referred to groups within a single species.<ref name="GG4">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''</ref>

==Classification==
{{Quote|There were green creatures with horns, brown creatures with flat-crooked heads, silver things with red things sticking out of blue things, big furry things, little furry things, creatures with big fish eyes, creatures with no eyes, and creatures with things that I couldn't even begin to describe.|[[Grael]] describes a wealth of species to [[Ponto]]|<ref name="Escape from Balis-Baurgh">{{JournalCite|1|Escape from Balis-Baurgh}}</ref>}}
[[File:Cw_horax.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A non-sentient [[Horax/Legends|horax]]]]
The five characteristics of life forms were: ''organization'' (a distinct form and appearance), ''irritability'' (the ability to respond to external stimuli), ''metabolism'' (the ability to convert energy to stay alive), ''reproduction'' (the ability to create new lifeforms), and ''adaptation'' (the ability to change as their environments change).<ref name="GG8">''[[Galaxy Guide 8: Scouts]]''</ref><ref name="AE">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref>

Species were divided into many categories, based on their various characteristics. [[Sentience/Legends|Sentience]] was a significant trait in describing life forms, as such, species were  divided into three groups based on their level of sentience: ''sentient'', ''semi-sentient'', and ''non-sentient''.<ref name="NEGtC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Another classification was based around the key element in the chemical structure of a life from: the predominant form of life in the galaxy was [[Carbon/Legends|carbon]]-based. Other forms of life existed, such as [[Silicon/Legends|silicon]]-based<ref name="Wildlife">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> or energy-based life forms.<ref name="AE" /> Reports from remote parts of the galaxy even mentioned giant clouds of interstellar gas which had evolved a form of intelligence based on internal force-fields.<ref name="SWOPM">[[Star Wars Official Poster Monthly 16|''Star Wars Official Poster Monthly'' 16]]</ref>

In describing eco-systems, life forms were divided into several major categories which included:

* ''[[Plant/Legends|Plants]]'', or ''Plant-based'', typically synthesized energy from [[Star/Legends|sunlight]] via [[Photosynthesis/Legends|photosynthesis]]. Plants were known to reproduce themselves and usually rooted into the ground<ref name="New Alien">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]</ref> being immobile, although some plant species were able to move to seek better soil, light and nutrients, or even to attack other life forms.<ref name="Tendrils">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=enemy|Tendril|[[Oricon]]}}</ref> Non-sentient plants, collectively - ''flora'' - included [[Tree/Legends|trees]], such as [[Blba tree/Legends|Blba tree]] or [[Wroshyr tree/Legends|Wroshyr tree]], [[Flower/Legends|flowers]], and various other kinds of life, such as [[Tendril]]s. Some examples of sentient plants were [[Neti/Legends|Neti]], [[Ergesh]], [[Revwien/Legends|Revwiens]], [[Zelosian]]s, [[Sylphe]].
* ''[[Fungus/Legends|Fungi]]'' typically obtained energy from digesting organic matter. Non-sentient fungi, collectively - ''funga'' - included [[Glowshroom|glowshrooms]], [[Klol fungus|klol]], [[Lokka Fungus|lokka]], [[Grenade fungi/Legends|grenade fungi]]. Some examples of sentient fungi were [[Unidentified Endor mushroom|Endor mushrooms]].
* ''Animals'', or ''creatures'', typically obtained energy from eating other life forms. Based on the type of life forms a creature would eat, a variety of [[Diet/Legends|dietary subcategories]] existed. Across all animals, the majority were [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]] breathers,<ref name="AE" /> although a number breathed other substances such as [[Ammonia/Legends|ammonia]], [[cyanogen]], [[Methane/Legends|methane]],<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref> [[methanogen]],<ref name="SOL">''[[Shield of Lies]]''</ref> [[Helium/Legends|helium]] and [[Dorin gas/Legends|Dorin gas]],<ref name="NEGtC" /> or did not require breathing at all.<ref name="New Alien" /> Non-sentient creatures were collectively known as ''fauna''.
* ''[[Virus (disambiguation)|Viruses]]'' were microorganisms that reproduced by infecting other life forms and exploited their inner systems to produce new copies of themselves. Some examples of viruses included [[Blue Shadow Virus/Legends|Blue Shadow virus]],<ref>{{TCW|Blue Shadow Virus (episode)}}</ref> [[Gobindi virus]]<ref name="GOF3">''[[Galaxy of Fear: Planet Plague]]''</ref> or bio-engineered [[Nanovirus|nanoviruses]].<ref name="ImpCom501st">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref>
* ''[[Bacteria/Legends|Bacteria]]'' were microscopic life forms.<ref name="GFT">''[[Galladinium's Fantastic Technology]]''</ref>

Species, and especially animals, were furtherly divided in a number ways, with separate categories often intercepting. 

===Based on living environment===
* ''Aquatic'' species were the marine life, or those descended from it. Aquatic lifeforms included those that could breathe [[Water/Legends|water]], air, or both. These included the sentient [[Herglic/Legends|Herglic]] and [[Swimming People of Dellalt|Dellaltian]]. 
* ''[[Amphibian/Legends|Amphibious]]'' species could live both in water and on land, or had separate water-based and land-based stages of life. Some were born as tadpoles possessing gills, and developed lungs to breathe air, while others had compound lungs that allowed them to breathe underwater and on land.<ref name="New Alien" /> These included the sentient [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]],<ref name="UAA" /> [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]].<ref name="GCG">''[[Galactic Campaign Guide]]''</ref>, [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]]<ref name="New Alien" /> and [[Nautolan/Legends|Nautolan]].<ref name="FaD">[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]]</ref>
* ''Arboreal'' species lived in [[Forest/Legends|forests]] and were especially adapted to [[Tree/Legends|tree]] living.<ref name="New Alien" />
[[File:Alien_lineup.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A group of sentients]]
===Based on internal characteristics===
* ''[[Vertebrate|Vertebrates]]''<ref name="New Alien" /> were species with bones and an inner skeletal frame.
** ''[[Mammal/Legends|Mammalian]]'' species were warm-blooded vertebrates, who typically bore live young, though some species lay eggs. Regardless of the birth process, a female mammal nourished young through [[Milk/Legends|secretions]] from ''mammary glands''. Most mammals were partially covered in [[Hair/Legends|hair]].<ref name="New Alien" /> Notable forms of sentient mammals were [[Human/Legends|Humans]], [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]], [[Cerean/Legends|Cereans]], [[Bothan/Legends|Bothans]] and [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustans]].
*** ''[[Monotreme]]''<ref name="Card-CCG-Kal'Falnl C'ndros">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Kal'Falnl C'ndros}}</ref> species were mammals that lay eggs.
*** ''[[Cetacean/Legends|Cetacean]]'' species were aquatic mammals, usually typified by a predominance of a hairless or nearly hairless body, anterior flipper-like limbs, vestigial posterior limbs, and a flat, notched tail.<ref name="New Alien" />
*** ''[[Primate/Legends|Primate]]'', or ''Simian'', species were mammalian [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]], exhibiting characteristics of [[Ape/Legends|apes]].<ref name="New Alien" /> Some of the most prominent species in the galaxy were primates, such as the [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and their numerous [[Near-Human|offshoots]].
** ''[[Bird/Legends|Avian]]'' species were warm-blooded, feathered and winged creatures, described as flying mammals.<ref name="New Alien" /> Avians were born from eggs. They typically had light bones and strong muscles, needed to enable flight. However, many avian species had lost the ability to fly. Examples of this kind included the sentient [[Vor]], [[Mrlssi]], [[Quor'sav/Legends|Quor'sav]], [[Rishii/Legends|Rishii]], [[S'kytri]], [[Fosh/Legends|Fosh]] and the [[Tikiarri]].
** ''[[Reptile/Legends|Reptilian]]'', or ''Saurian'', species were cold-blooded vertebrates, typically covered in scales or bony plates. They were mostly land-based and reproduced by laying fertilized eggs. Some could change color to match their environment.<ref name="New Alien" /> The group included [[Lizard/Legends|lizards]], [[Snake/Legends|snakes]] and [[crocodile]]s, as well sentients like the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodians]], [[Barabel/Legends|Barabels]], [[Chistori]], and [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshans]]. Reptile sentients also came in less [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] forms, such as the [[Slith]] and [[Ssi-ruu]].
*** ''[[Reptavian/Legends|Reptavian]]'' species were flying reptiles.<ref name="New Alien" /> Notable reptavian species were [[Thranta/Legends|thrantas]].<ref name="Wildlife" />
*** ''[[Reptomammal/Legends|Reptomammal]]'' species were reptiles that reproduced through birth rather than laying eggs. These included sentient [[Vurk/Legends|Vurk]].<ref name="New Alien" />
** ''[[Craniopod]]'' species were an exotic group that included sentient humanoids [[Bith/Legends|Bith]].<ref name="Databank">{{DB|species|bith|Bith}}</ref> 
* ''Hard [[Invertebrate/Legends|invertebrates]]'' had hard outer bodies with no internal skeleton. Examples of hard invertebrate sentient species included the [[Sauvax]], the [[Aganof]], the [[Tarc]] and the [[Sarlacc/Legends|Sarlacc]].
** ''[[Arthropod/Legends|Arthropods]]''
*** ''[[Crustacean/Legends|Crustacean]]'' species were aquatic [[Lobster/Legends|lobster]]-like arthropods or shellfish that usually had a segmented body, a chitinous exoskeleton, and paired, jointed limbs.<ref name="New Alien" />
*** ''[[Insect/Legends|Insectoid]]'', or ''insect'', species were arthropods<ref name="Dark Nest I: The Joiner King">''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]'', Chapter 8.</ref> with defined body segments; most commonly head, thorax and abdomen, though some insectoid species evolved into different forms, such as humanoid insect species. Common characteristics of insects included a chitinous shell, multiple legs (typically 2 or 6), antennae, and multifaceted eyes.<ref name="New Alien" /> Many insect species had wings. Common sentient examples of this form of life were the [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]], [[Fefze]], [[Killik/Legends|Killik]], [[Bartokk]], [[Gand/Legends|Gand]], and [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosians]].
*** ''[[Spider/Legends|Arachnids]]<ref name="AE" />
* ''Soft [[Invertebrate/Legends|invertebrates]]'' were descended from soft-bodied species with no hard carcass at all, such as [[Slug (creature)/Legends|slugs]] and [[Worm/Legends|worms]]. Sentient species of this origin took many diverse forms, such as the [[Ee]] and [[Celegian/Legends|Celegians]].<ref name="UAA" />
** ''[[Cephalopod/Legends|Cephalopod]]'' species bore the traits inherent in most [[Squid/Legends|squid]] and [[Octopus/Legends|octopi]], namely water-based or amphibious creatures with tentacles.<ref name="New Alien" /> These included sentient [[Iyra]].<ref name="GG4b">[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races'', Second Edition]]</ref>
** ''[[Gastropod/Legends|Gastropod]]'' species moved by means of a wide muscular foot, or their whole body acted as one. These included sentient [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]].<ref name="New Alien" />
[[File:Alien_lineup2.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Another group of sentients]]
===Based on visual image===
* ''[[Canine/Legends|Canine]]'' species possessed some characteristics of the [[Dog/Legends|dog]] family, including a pronounced muzzle, sharp teeth, advanced hunting and tracking instincts, sharp teeth, claws, padded feet, and a tail.<ref name="New Alien" />
* ''[[Rodent/Legends|Rodent]]'' species had characteristics of [[Mouse/Legends|mice]] or [[Rat/Legends|rats]], also including gnawing or nibbling mammals with continuously growing incisors.<ref name="New Alien" />
* ''[[Feline/Legends|Feline]]'' species had characteristics of the [[Cat/Legends|cat]] family, such as extremely flexible body, sharp teeth, slit-pupiled eyes, a tail, and padded, clawed digits.<ref name="New Alien" />
* ''[[Humanoid/Legends|Humanoid]]'' species, while not always genetically related to [[Human/Legends|Humans]], possessed characteristics similar to Humans, such as two arms with hands, fingers and an opposable thumb, two legs, a torso, and a single head.<ref name="New Alien" />
* ''[[Porcine/Legends|Porcine]]'' species had the characteristic of a [[Swine|pig]], sometimes including a blunt-ended nose, tusks and hooves.<ref name="New Alien" />

However some species were very hard to classify, such as the [[Filar-Nitzan/Legends|Filar-Nitzan]], the [[Pulra]], or the living planets [[Hemes Arbora]].

== History ==
The earliest known genesis of life in the [[The galaxy/Legends|Galaxy]] took place on the planet [[Goroth Prime/Legends|Goroth Prime]] [[5,000,000,000 BBY|5,000,000,000 years before]] the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], as it was estimated by [[Xenobiologist/Legends|scientists]] during the reign if the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="GSE5">''[[Goroth: Slave of the Empire]]''</ref> By [[3,000,000 BBY]] life already thrived on [[Vinsoth/Legends|Vinsoth]] and by [[2,000,000 BBY]] on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]].<ref name="New Alien" /> 

However, with the appearance of advanced interstellar civilizations, the natural development of life became severally influenced by scientific experiments and conception of artificial species,<ref name="codex mother machine">{{TORcite|type=codex|Mother Machine}}</ref> terraforming<ref name="KotOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> and transplantation of life stock<ref name="New Alien" /> or war beasts.<ref name="Barely">{{SW|url=news/barely-tolerable-alien-henchmen-of-the-empire-part-2|series=Barely Tolerable: Alien Henchmen of the Empire|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref> Because of this, while some species had a well-known world of origin, such as [[Thranta/Legends|thrantas]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]],<ref name="codex thranta">{{TORcite|type=codex|Thranta}}</ref> other species' native origin was unknown and specimens of the same or closely-related species could be found across the [[The galaxy/Legends|Galaxy]] on worlds that didn't have direct contact for millennia. An example of such creatures were [[Mewvorr]]s, found around the time of the [[Galactic War]] on both [[Zakuul]] and [[Voss]], when these two planets were rediscovered for the first time in centuries.<ref name="TOR">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=location|[[Voss]] and [[Zakuul]]}}</ref>

==The study of species==
{{Quote|In our efforts, we have learned that life is not rare. Rather, given a chance, ''life will occur''. It is tenacious, aggressive&mdash;it seems to crave existence.|[[Tem Eliss]], [[sentientologist]]|<ref name="GG12">''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]''</ref>}}
A scientific discipline of studying various species of organisms was called ''[[xenobiology]]'', also known as ''xenology'' or ''biology''. Multiple branches of xenobiology focusing on specific groups of life existed, such as [[Zoologist/Legends|''zoology'']] - the study of animals, ''[[botany]]'' - the study of plants,<ref name="GatORWp54">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> and ''[[mycology]]'' - the study of fungi.<ref name="fungal protection">{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=dynamic|Fungal Protection|[[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]]}}</ref>

The [[Shi'ido]] researcher [[Mammon Hoole]] wrote the acclaimed ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''. He gained unique insights into species by infiltration using his shapeshifting abilities.<ref name="EGAS" /> Other documents that detailed various species included the ''[[Universal Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="SWOPM" />

===The study of sentients===
[[File:Tem_Ellis.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Tem Eliss, a notable sentientologist]]
{{Quote|Skynx, there're more life forms in this galaxy than anyone's bothered to count, you know that. Just listing the sentient ones is a life's work.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], to [[S. V. Skynx/Legends|S. V. Skynx]]|<ref name="The Lost Legacy">''[[Han Solo and the Lost Legacy]]''</ref>}}
Study of sentient species was called ''[[sentientology]]'', and [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] that studied sentient species were known as [[sentientologist]]s.<ref name="GG4" /> Many institutions in the galaxy focused on the study of sentient species. The most notable were the [[University of Coruscant/Legends|University of Coruscant]]<ref name="EGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> and the [[University of Sanbra]].<ref name="GG4" />

One of the major works on sentientology, [[Obo Rin]]'s ''[[Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy]]'', was commissioned by Lord [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Vader]], and was carried out under the auspices of [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[Vontenn]], Liaison Officer of Sentiology Studies. While it contained much information, it was also a conduit for Imperial [[Propaganda/Legends|propaganda]], and as such, had a tendency to depict some species as less developed than was actually the case.<ref name="GG4" /> Rin's credentials as a scientist were also questionable.<ref name="GG41">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]'', first edition</ref>

Another major work on sentientology was ''[[The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life]]'' by the [[Iyra]] [[Tem Eliss]]. Rather than a scientific study, it was designed to facilitate first contact with species, providing "guidelines as to common cultural interests, goals, fears and drives." However, it departed from Imperial doctrine on a number of points. The Empire tried to apprehend its author shortly before publication, but the academic escaped and released his research through underground networks and [[NewsNet]]s.<ref name="GG12" />

==Behind the scenes==
Species in the ''Star Wars'' universe generally have a large compatibility to real-world classification systems. However, these are not always strictly adhered to, because unlike in real-world modern biology, most categories of species in ''Star Wars'' universe are descriptive and not ancestral. As such, groups like "feline" include creatures of various real-world classes, from mammalian [[Nexu/Legends|Nexu]] to non-mammalian [[Mawvorr]].<ref name="Voss feline">{{TORcite|type=other|Achievement: "Voss Feline Handler"}}</ref>  Numerous species shared characteristics from different classifications, such as the [[Quor'sav/Legends|Quor'sav]] species with both mammalian and avian features<ref name="Card-CCG-Kal'Falnl C'ndros" /> or [[Opee sea killer/Legends|Opee]] with both crustacean and fish features.<ref name="Wildlife" />

According to ''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]'', the [[Colossus wasp/Legends|Colossus wasps]] "follow the standard insect physiognomy, with a head, thorax and abdomen,"<ref name="The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels">''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]'', 88.</ref> which corresponds with the real-world physiognomy of insects;<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/insect|text=Insect|work=Dictionary.com|archivedate=20111015234255}}</ref> however, the [[Sic-Six/Legends|Sic-Six]], which also have these three body segments but eight legs, are classified as arachnids,<ref name="GG4" /> which in the real world have only two body segments.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/arachnid|text=Arachnid|work=[http://dictionary.reference.com Dictionary.com]|archivedate=20111015031827}}</ref>
